current_text.html: A particular church which is not incorporated, desiring to elect trustees, may select from among its membership trustees or officers of like nature who shall have the power and authority: a. to buy, sell, or mortgage property for the church, b. to accept and execute deeds as such trustees, c. to hold and defend titles to the same, and d. to manage any permanent special funds entrusted to them for the furtherance of the purposes of the church. In the fulfillment of their duties, such trustees shall be subject always to the authority, and shall act solely under the instructions of the congregation which they serve as trustees. The powers or duties of such trustees must not infringe upon the powers or duties of the Session or of the Board of Deacons. Such trustees shall be elected in regularly constituted congregational meetings.

metadata.synopsis: A presbytery annulled a session's actions after the session added to a petition-called congregational meeting a recommendation that the congregation invoke BCO 24-6 against eleven elders. The SJC sustained the session's complaint: BCO 25-2 permits a session to add agenda items, and BCO 24-6 does not require a member-initiated motion; the congregation's own 503–229 vote began the process. It reinstated the session's actions, declared remaining relief moot, and noted one recorded dissent; no dissent text appears.
